## Discovery & Translational Science

* **Ciguatoxin cardiotoxicity driven by RyR2-dependent calcium leak** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.31.748269)
  * Experimental studies in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived ventricular cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) and rat models showed purified ciguatoxins (CTX-1B and CTX-3C) induce rapid diastolic intracellular `[Ca²⁺]` alterations and RyR2-dependent calcium leaks.
  * Ciguatoxin exposure led to severe excitation-contraction coupling disruption and sarcomeric disorganization, identifying RyR2 channel dysregulation as the primary molecular driver of ciguatera-related cardiac dysfunction.

* **High-throughput screen identifies dengue virus NS5 methyltransferase inhibitors** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.org/42697293/)
  * Researchers established a bioluminescence-based high-throughput screening platform to identify direct-acting small-molecule inhibitors targeting the NS5 methyltransferase of the dengue virus.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **Topical tripelennamine demonstrates anti-pruritic efficacy in proof-of-concept trial** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.01.26361939)
  * A single-center, double-blind, randomized crossover trial (n = 36) evaluated 1% tripelennamine (TPA) cream versus 1% diphenhydramine (DPH) and vehicle control in histamine-induced pruritus.
  * Pretreatment with 1% TPA significantly reduced histamine-induced area under the curve for visual analog scale itch (AUC-VAS) and total itch duration compared to vehicle control.

* **Transcranial photobiomodulation restores cortical alpha power and working memory in ADHD** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.01.26361884)
  * A double-blind, sham-controlled crossover trial evaluated 16-minute sessions of 150 mW right prefrontal transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM) in 28 adults with ADHD versus 29 healthy controls.
  * Active tPBM significantly improved working memory K scores and induced electroencephalography changes, including increased relative alpha power and neural complexity across frontoparietal attention networks.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Bristol Myers Squibb pauses Phase 1 CAR-T clinical study** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/09/04/pharmalittle-bristol-car-t-trial-pause-pfizer-offloads-shelved-candidate/)
  * Bristol Myers Squibb has placed an early-stage CAR-T clinical program on pause, according to industry updates.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

* **[Big Pharma]** **Novartis and Ionis candidate pelacarsen fails pivotal trial** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/04/novartis-therapy-pelacarsen-fails-cardiovascular-trial/)
  * Pelacarsen, an antisense oligonucleotide targeting apolipoprotein(a) co-developed with Ionis Pharmaceuticals, failed to meet its primary endpoint in a pivotal Phase 3 cardiovascular outcomes trial.
  * The outcome represents a major setback for Novartis’s late-stage cardiovascular pipeline targeting lipoprotein(a) reduction.

* **[Big Pharma]** **AbbVie bispecific etentamig meets primary endpoint in Phase 3 multiple myeloma trial** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/abbvie-multiple-myeloma-etentamig-phase-3-trial-results/829672/)
  * Etentamig, a dual-acting bispecific antibody binding tumor cells and T cells, met its primary progression-free survival (PFS) endpoint in patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma who progressed on two or more prior lines of therapy.
  * Safety findings highlighted low rates of cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), potentially enabling outpatient administration in community oncology settings.

* **[Biotech]** **Summit Therapeutics reports Phase 3 overall survival gains for ivonescimab** [X / ApexOnco](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2095909018371776914)
  * Summit Therapeutics observed positive overall survival trends in the Harmoni and Harmoni-2 Phase 3 trials evaluating ivonescimab in non-small cell lung cancer ahead of upcoming presentations at WCLC 2026.

## Regulatory & Approvals

* **[Big Pharma]** **FDA grants accelerated approval to AstraZeneca’s Etcamah (camizestrant)** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-grants-accelerated-approval-new-breast-cancer-treatment)
  * The FDA approved Etcamah (camizestrant), an oral selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD), in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib, palbociclib, or ribociclib) for adults with HR⁺/HER2⁻ locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer harboring ESR1 mutations upon progression on prior endocrine and CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy.
  * Approval was supported by the SERENA-6 trial; the Guardant360 CDx liquid biopsy was concurrently approved as a companion diagnostic device to detect ESR1 mutations.

* **[Biotech]** **FDA approves Ionis Pharmaceuticals’ Zanvastro for Alexander disease** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/ionis-rare-neurology-drug-approved-pfizer-inks-an-adc-deal/829639/)
  * Zanvastro received FDA approval as the first disease-modifying therapy for Alexander disease, designed to suppress production of a protein that forms toxic clumps damaging the central nervous system.
  * Approval was based on functional clinical data demonstrating motor stabilization in a timed walking test, earning Ionis a Priority Review Voucher.

* **[Big Pharma]** **FDA rescinds accelerated approval for BMS’s Krazati in colorectal cancer** [X / Jacob Plieth](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2095982820611043805)
  * The FDA formally rescinded the accelerated approval indication for Krazati (adagrasib) in KRAS G12C-mutated colorectal cancer following the failure of the confirmatory Phase 3 KRYSTAL-10 trial.

* **FDA issues emergency compounding guidance for neonatal parenteral nutrition** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-takes-steps-maintain-newborn-access-life-saving-starter-nutrition-products)
  * The FDA issued immediate-implementation guidance describing regulatory priorities for compounding starter parenteral nutrition products for neonates to prevent supply gaps caused by the permanent closure of two major compounding outsourcing facilities.

## Business & Strategy

* **[Biotech]** **Medicus Pharma licenses discontinued anti-CD228 ADC from Pfizer** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/ionis-rare-neurology-drug-approved-pfizer-inks-an-adc-deal/829639/)
  * Medicus Pharma entered into a licensing agreement with Pfizer to acquire rights to an anti-CD228 antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) for $12 million upfront and an additional $15 million due in one year.
  * Pfizer had previously terminated a Phase 1 dose-escalation trial for the program after enrolling 11 patients.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Western pharma licensing of Chinese biotech assets maintains high momentum** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/charts-biotech-deals-china-alumis-ultragenyx-stock/829635/)
  * Cross-border licensing activity between Western drug developers and Chinese biotechs continues at high volumes in 2026, driven by recent large-scale agreements from firms including GSK (Hutchmed) and Roche (Simcere Pharmaceutical).

## Public Health & Policy

* **Epidemiological modeling evaluates monthly oral PrEP deployment in Sub-Saharan Africa** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.01.26361983)
  * An agent-based network model evaluated the 2026–2035 scale-up of MK-8527, an experimental monthly oral HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) candidate, in South Africa and Kenya.
  * Assuming 95% efficacy, monthly oral MK-8527 alone is projected to avert 6%–14% of new HIV infections, serving as a low-cost, self-administered alternative or complement to injectable lenacapavir.

**Worth watching:** Detailed overall survival data for Summit Therapeutics' ivonescimab at WCLC 2026 following its Phase 3 readouts against standard-of-care regimens in non-small cell lung cancer.

youtube.markdown:
- Biology & Health
    - [Modifiable lifestyle interventions for migraine | Brian Grosberg, M.D.](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/-Kw_gxbnoIc) -- Peter Attia MD
        - Frames migraine as a distinct neurological disease rather than a standard headache, changing how clinicians understand and treat the condition.
        - Outlines the multi-phase progression of migraines, from prodromal warning signs up to 24 hours prior to postdromal cognitive fog.
        - Addresses why cluster headaches—among the most painful medical conditions—are frequently misdiagnosed as sinus infections or allergies.
        - Examines the hereditary and demographic patterns of migraine, including a strong familial link and a female prevalence roughly three times higher than in men.
    - [The phases of migraine | Brian Grosberg, M.D.](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/AmSEX2qIv_U) -- Peter Attia MD
        - Differentiates migraine as a complex neurological disease instead of an ordinary headache, altering therapeutic and diagnostic paradigms.
        - Covers the full timeline of migraine phases, spanning early warning signs a day prior to lingering brain fog following pain resolution.
        - Explores why cluster headaches are commonly misattributed to allergies or sinus issues despite their distinct severity.
        - Discusses genetic predisposition in families and the biological factors leading to a 3:1 female-to-male ratio in migraine incidence.
    - [OpenEvidence & Digital Health Inside Out | HealthTech #DadJokes](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Q0Sgk6yqg0U) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Features episode #11 of the weekly "HealthTech Dad Jokes" short-form video series hosted by Alex Koshykov and Sergei Polevikov.
        - Presents comedic content and jokes focused on the healthcare AI platform OpenEvidence and the channel itself.
        - Targets professionals across digital health, healthcare AI, health IT, medical startups, hospitals, and venture capital.
- Pure Science
    - [What Is Math For in the Age of AI? - Live from ICM 2026 | PODCAST: The Joy of Why](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IXwrLMtuv4Q) -- Quanta Magazine
        - Features a live recording from the 2026 International Congress of Mathematicians hosted by Steven Strogatz and Janna Levin, with guests Akshay Venkatesh, Ravi Vakil, and Alex Kontorovich.
        - Highlights recent AI milestones such as AlphaProof's performance at the IMO and automated proofs of Erdős problems that demonstrate machines generating formal proofs and linking disparate math fields.
        - Discusses the human value of mathematics beyond mechanical proof production, focusing on mathematical intuition, "moral truth," storytelling, and the "forklift analogy" regarding human struggle.
        - Analyzes practical effects of AI on mathematics education and research, including shifts in test scores, open-source tool accessibility, and career trajectories for graduate students.
    - [EL NIÑO : Pourquoi l'Océan Pacifique bascule-t-il ?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DutKGuQu4a0) -- ScienceEtonnante
        - Investigates the geophysical and oceanographic mechanisms driving the El Niño phenomenon in the tropical Pacific Ocean.
        - Analyzes the baseline structural dynamics of the tropical Pacific and explains how ocean-atmosphere coupling breaks down during El Niño events.
        - Details the physical framework of the recharge oscillator model, covering the ocean's thermal discharge and recharge cycles.
        - Outlines the broader ecological and global climate consequences resulting from these Pacific oceanographic shifts.
- Tech & Engineering
    - [How the Channel Tunnel Works](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gLkbK8h_9fc) -- Wendover Productions
        - The video description provides promotional links for Nebula subscriptions, including a 50% discount on annual plans and access to Day Pass.
        - Writing for the video was done by Sam Denby, Tristan Purdy, and Christine Benedetti, with video editing handled by Alexander Williard.
        - Animation was produced by Sara Stoltman, Gabriel Ferreras, Austin Glass, and Kate Ermolenkko, with sound design by Manni Simon and Dony Bullen.
